<thought>We need the number of distinct proton environments in the target compound. The only way to get that information is to obtain its ¹H NMR spectrum, which lists the signals corresponding to chemically equivalent hydrogens. The tool `proton_nmr_spectra` provides this spectrum for the compound in question (the SMILES is pre‑loaded in the environment, so no arguments are required). We'll call the tool, then count the separate signals in the returned spectrum.</thought>
<action>proton_nmr_spectra</action>
